    Beware: Devices meant to make people safe may be dangerous to immigrants

    manilateam Posted on September 29, 2026
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 9:31
    Instaread

    By Cesar Antonio Nucum Jr.
    SAN FRANCISCO – There is a growing danger to privacy and civil liberty as the immigration crackdown continues.
    This appears to be the concern of many following the San Francisco American Community Media briefing on the topic “The Expanding Surveillance Dragnet — Stealth Chapter in the War on Immigrants” moderated by AcoM Executive Director Jaya Padmanabhan.
    The ominous danger to privacy and civil liberty concern includes the seeming creepy violation to the Fourth Amendment of the U.S. Constitution against unreasonable search and seizure by the government.
    Focusing on the resistance to the tactics of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and proliferation of surveillance tools from Automated License Plate Readers (ALPR) system to cell site stimulators that has become an eyeopener to many, speakers at the briefing gave brighter perspectives on how the devices supposedly help in amber alerts or locating a missing child, the location of stolen vehicles, and fleeing usually hit-and-run suspects, among others are, in turn, being used particularly against members of the immigration community.

    During these times of apparent more intensive crackdown on illegal immigration that had anti-ICE activists more concerned and prompted them to wanting the alarmed immigrant communities not just to be on their toes but also vigilant and be active to counteract these unlawful stalking as what ALPRs by Flock Safety, a widespread supposedly connected public safety platform.

    Former Flock employee turned whistleblower, presently an immigrant rights activist and community organizer Jonathan Paz admitted that he thought that technology that can help safe solve crime issues had for its “main role is to surveil the public Americans and they’re basically work around public and legal scrutiny.”

    “Flock and its other similar surveillance companies like Rekor Systems, Vigilant Solutions Video Systems, and Axon Fusus are meant to spy. They are supposed to have safeguards, don’t sell the data they gathered, that these things they have are supposed to protect but these weren’t the case. These companies were indirectly and directly violating state laws. It was basically revealed that in Illinois that border patrol had access and was getting access to their data against their own data sharing laws and privacy laws,” Paz revealed. “In California many cities have access to your systems to do immigration enforcements and there was virtually no accountability. The Fourth Amendment is mythical as it is basically dead as they are also immune to statewide scrutiny.”

    Paz also warned that once the cameras go up, “it’s very hard to control how the local law enforcement agencies use them because who’s policing the police, the sheriff” as they’re the ones auditing themselves.

    “Instead of making us safer these technologies are being used to abduct, kidnap our neighbors supporting the work of Department of Homeland Security (DHS) ICE Border Patrol. These things are being weaponized and they’re being weaponized across the country,” Paz lamented.

    It is estimated that there are about 120,000 Flock cameras performing some two billion scans every month but only 1% of these incidents that have been identified actually have resulted in some follow-up action like a kidnapping.

    Secure Justice executive Director Brian Hofer sustained Paz’s information and shared that he is presently working on the strategies of coalition building and litigation as public pressure have become truly effective.

    “In the entire Flock system, it’s so much more than just a license plate number that you often hear especially with AI the synthesis of public data and private data that is all being fused together in these analytics programs and, with the power of AI and essentially unlimited data, they are able to get the ability to profile and locate people very quickly and, unfortunately, extremely easy.” Hofer said. “In Oakland, California alone, there have been 4.4 million illegal searches, 638 million plate scans and an average of around 210,000 third-party searches per month.”

    Hofer also reported that in 2016 or 2017, their group told the State of California that ICE has direct access to the DMV after the “wonderfully intended thing of creating a special driver’s license for undocumented so that they can get insurance and not feel afraid is a well-intended idea, but nobody turned off the pipeline.”

    “We told them that you are going to put all these people at risk with this data because it’s going out to this private nonprofit party. So sure enough, ICE start showing up to people’s doors. They were targeting people because we help them self-identify as being undocumented. Thankfully, that there was a legislative fix the following year, but that’s a whole year of risk that never needed to happen,” Hofer narrated.

    Services Immigrant Rights and Education Network (SIREN) San Jose City-based community organizer Kimberly Woo readily stated that “no matter how perfect the policy, the current federal government has no bounds to lawless terror and we have seen and experienced how the government will weaponize any tool against our people.”

    “The federal government now has over $240 billion to waste on immigration enforcement that tears apart entire communities separates our families and destabilizes our economies. This government invests money to profiteer companies like Palantir to act as bounty hunters using AI powered tools that collect data from both private and public sources to fuel the mass deportation machine and to line the corporate pockets. So whether it be DMV driver, data voting records, taxpayer information, TSA reports, healthcare information, among other,” Woo shared. “Federal government has abused our private data to detain and deport our community. Information that people and our community members have basically shared in order to access benefits and services that they were eligible for is now being thrown against them into the communities.”

    Woo told of how she had loved ones who when in a final green card interview had their hands and feet handcuffed by ICE agents and forcefully shipped one of them to Mesa Verde and the other to the state’s largest lawless detention facility in California.

    “In a matter of days one of my loved ones was forcibly deported and said goodbye to the future they waited more than 20 years and weeks later their partner decided to self-report due to the heartbreaking suffocating conditions of detention. Their detention marked the first time my loved ones spent a night apart and their decades long marriage,” sadly related Woo. “And that’s the goal of detention deportation family separation and collective fear. My family even feared applying to eligible programs or even to renew their green cards legal documents that they are bound by because they are fearing that our data will be weaponized against them. And I really want to underscore that mass surveillance does not keep us safe. In fact it keeps us afraid.”

    Immigrant Legal Resource Center’s Lena Graber who has been working in immigrant rights and immigration enforcement for nearly two decades stated that the U.S. immigration system was a deeply racist and punitive legal regime long before the Donald Trump era “but nothing in history can compare to what’s been happening in the immigration system in the last year or two.”

    Graber added that the last two years have seen just record-breaking changes in the way that immigration law and policy work to make the system infinitely more vicious and dehumanizing.

    “Aside from using immigration as the front line of authoritarianism the Trump administration is on a merciless mission to deport as many people as they can and to make it as hard as possible for people to come here or to live here to make them as miserable as possible to deter all immigration. Almost every day they come out with another rule or another policy that makes it harder to get legal status that takes away immigrant rights that restricts protective procedures in immigration court and that makes the detention and deportation system more cruel and inhumane,” Graber described.

    “California has 25% of all of the immigrants in the country but accounted for only 8% of ICE arrests so far. An immigrant is four times as likely to be arrested by ICE in Texas as in California. In Wyoming 14 out of every 100 immigrants was arrested in 2026 while only .2 were out of a hundred were arrested in Illinois. In other words, sanctuary policies do work. That’s part of why the Trump administration hates them so much,” Graber indicated.

    Graber believes that ICE’s goal is to figure out who among they took pictures of is subject to deportation who is potentially subject to deportation and then go and arrest those people and deport them.

    “It was established in 2009 or 10 when DHS decided that ICE would automatically receive the fingerprints of every single person arrested anywhere in the country regardless of the basis or the pretext for that arrest. This gives enormous power to local police over immigration enforcement because they know all they have to do to potentially get someone deported is to bring them into custody, whether or not charges are ever filed, that that person’s fingerprints go to ICE. And this still happens everywhere, every day even in sanctuary jurisdictions.,” Graber rued.

    Garber also put the blame of what is happening not just on Trump’s completely trampling the rule of law as legislators have given his administration the money to do it making them complicit too and that “organizing together we can build power and momentum to fight authoritarianism at large and bring back democratic governance.”
